problems.statement: What can be seen on the Moon's sky more often – the Sun or the Earth?

solution.statement: The Moon has a synodic period (i.e. period of rotation relative to the Sun) of 29.53 days. Therefore the Sun is visible from any place of the lunar surface during periods of about 2 weeks. Between these periods it will be under the horizon for about 2 weeks. As for the Earth, the situation is different: the Earth is always visible from the side of the Moon that can be seen from the Earth, but from the other side it is never seen. It means that one can see the Earth more often from the visible side of the Moon, and only the Sun from the other side.

problems.statement: A new postal service is established. A huge cannon shots a postal shell from England to New Zealand. Estimate the duration of the shell's flight.

solution.statement: England and New Zealand are located on opposite points of the Earth. Therefore the shell's trajectory will be close to half of the minimal circular orbit of an artificial Earth satellite which duration is 1.5 h («Gagarin flight»). Therefore the ballistic flight of the postal shell takes about 45 min.

problems.statement: It is known that the equatorial coordinates of the vernal equinox point are $0\,\mathrm{hr}$ and $0\,\mathrm{deg}$. What are the coordinates of the north ecliptic pole?

solution.statement: Taking into account the value of inclination of the Earth rotation axis ($\varepsilon=23.5^\circ$) we can see that the North ecliptic pole coordinates are: right ascension of $18^{\mathrm h}$ and declination of $66.5^\circ$.

problems.statement: Suppose that the Sun collapsed suddenly to a black hole. How would the Earth's orbital period be affected?

solution.statement: If the Sun does not eject mass and does not irradiate gravitational waves during the collapse, its mass doesn't change. So the Earth orbit doesn't change either.

problems.statement: Is it possible the lunar Mare Crisium whose diameter is $520\,\mathrm{km}$, to be resolved by naked eye?

solution.statement:
The Moon diameter is $3476\,\mathrm{km}$, and the visible angular diameter of the lunar disk is $31'$. Therefore, the maximum visible diameter of the Mare Crisium is

$$31'\times520/3476=4.6'.$$

This is 3–5 times more than the angular resolution limit of a naked eye. Indeed, good observers can see the Mare Crisium, that was proofed by the pretelescopic draws of the Moon.

problems.statement: In the elliptical galaxy M32 (a satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy) there are about 250 million stars. The galaxy's visual brightness is of $9\,\mathrm{mag}$. If we assume that all stars there have equal luminosities, what would be the visual magnitude of one of the stars in the galaxy?

solution.statement: We can represent the figure 250 million $2.5\times100\times100\times100\times100$ which is equivalent to $1^{\mathrm m}+5^{\mathrm m}+5^{\mathrm m}+5^{\mathrm m}+5^{\mathrm m}=21^{\mathrm m}$. Therefore one star has brightness of $9^{\mathrm m}+21^{\mathrm m}=30^{\mathrm m}$.
